problemStatement.formal: \forall (E : \mathrm{InnerProductSpace}\ \mathbb{C}) (f\, g : E),\ \langle f,\, g\rangle = (\|f+g\|^{2} - \|f-g\|^{2} + i\,\|f+ig\|^{2} - i\,\|f-ig\|^{2})/4
problemStatement.plain: Formalize the complex polarization identity: the inner product on a complex Hilbert space is determined by four squared-norm values via ⟨f,g⟩ = (‖f+g‖² - ‖f-g‖² + i‖f+ig‖² - i‖f-ig‖²)/4.
whyMatters: Together with the (real) polarization identity already in the gallery, this lemma shows that the norm completely determines the inner product on every complex Hilbert space.
Many uniqueness arguments for unitary operators (polar decomposition, Mazur-Ulam, GNS construction) start from polarization, so a typed Mathlib-ready proof gives the gallery a clean entry point.
Completes the OQ-02 inner-product-from-norm program for the field ℂ; the OQ-02 parent already contains the ℝ-version.

proven: Mathlib upstream: inner_eq_sum_norm_sq_div_four in Mathlib.Analysis.InnerProductSpace.Basic — the identical statement over RCLike 𝕜 (specializes to both ℝ and ℂ via RCLike.I).
Gallery (cauchy-schwarz-oq-02 parent file CauchySchwarzOQ02.lean:161): polarization_identity (real case) ⟨f,g⟩_ℝ = (‖f+g‖² - ‖f-g‖²)/4, proven by norm_add_sq_real + norm_sub_sq_real + ring.
